findings.title: Installer check is skipped when no Integration record exists yet
findings.body: The new sender check (lines 501-505) runs only after the `except Integration.DoesNotExist` branch above has returned. When no Integration row exists for the installation_id (the installation webhook has not been processed, or never reaches Sentry, e.g. a self-hosted instance without webhook delivery), this line returns pipeline.next_step() immediately. The OAuth-authenticated GitHub user is never compared with the user who installed the app, and build_integration then links the installation to the org. test_basic_flow exercises exactly this path (no webhook posted, authenticated user 'octocat', no check), so the PR's main guarantee does not hold in the default path. Someone handed an installation_id belonging to another GitHub account can complete the install whenever the webhook record has not landed yet. The installer must be verified on this path too, or the pipeline must fail closed.

findings.title: KeyError when an existing Integration has no sender metadata
findings.body: integration.metadata['sender']['login'] assumes every existing Integration has a 'sender' entry. build_integration only writes sender when state.get('sender') is truthy (lines 376-377), so Integrations created by the pipeline without a webhook-provided sender, or created before this metadata existed, lack the key. For such a row that is ACTIVE but has no OrganizationIntegration, this line raises KeyError and the request returns a 500 instead of the error template. Use a safe lookup and treat a missing sender as a failed verification that renders the error page.

findings.title: Integration lookup is not scoped to the GitHub provider
findings.body: Both lookups by external_id=installation_id (this one and the one at line 478) omit provider=GitHubIntegrationProvider.key. external_id is only unique per provider, so the row found may belong to another provider and has no GitHub 'sender' in its metadata. The new check then indexes metadata['sender'] on a non-GitHub integration. Before this PR that case fell through to next_step. Add the provider filter to the lookup.

findings.title: Network and HTTP failures in the OAuth exchange escape as 500s
findings.body: safe_urlopen (line 423) is outside the try block, so a connection error or timeout raises out of the view instead of rendering the failure template; the try only guards reading the body. get_user_info (line 434) is also unguarded, so if it raises on a non-2xx response or on undecodable JSON, the user gets a 500 rather than the 'could not verify' page. Wrap the token exchange and user lookup and route failures to error(...).

findings.title: No test covers a successful install through the sender check or the new OAuth failure branches
findings.body: test_basic_flow never posts an installation webhook, so it never reaches the Integration-exists branch with a matching sender. The only test of that branch (test_github_user_mismatch) covers rejection. Nothing verifies that the matching installer is accepted with the check active. The new OAuth failure branches (state mismatch at integration.py line 412, missing access_token at line 431, missing login at line 435) have no tests either. Add a case that posts the installation event with sender 'octocat' (the stubbed /user login) and expects success, plus cases for a bad state and a failed token exchange.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the not-found path
findings.body: The test now sends a wrong state (ddd023...), so it fails at OAuthLoginView's state check and returns 'Invalid installation request.'. The original assertion for 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' (the 404 branch in build_integration, integration.py line 356) is no longer exercised anywhere in this file, despite the test name. Restore that assertion using the valid state, and keep the bad-state case as a separate test.

findings.title: Mismatch test asserts only a generic error that every failure path shares
findings.body: The mismatch test asserts only 'Invalid installation request.', which is the message for every failure in this pipeline: state mismatch, failed token exchange, missing login, missing Integration, and sender mismatch. It would still pass if the OAuth exchange broke, so it does not prove the sender check fired. It also does not assert that no OrganizationIntegration was created for org_2, which is the security-relevant outcome. Assert the absence of the OrganizationIntegration and/or give the sender mismatch its own error text.
